Good morning friends. **Prem** here, reporting on the ground from Michigan on
a long-awaited 2026 Election Day - and we find out just how tired Americans
are of **Donald Trump 's** authoritarian presidency and Republican control in
Washington.

In today's **' First Draft,'** I bring you a story the corporate media has
refused to touch this campaign season: We've seen the state obliterate free
speech and unconditionally fund a genocidal government all under the flag of
"Jewish safety." But what, if anything, is being done about _Arab and Muslim
safety_?

Plus, Trump's pals at the Supreme Court reject his request to set aside 20,000
ballots in California, the president is ready to preemptively pardon Elon
Musk, and a pardoned Jan. 6 defendant is charged with threatening to kill
judges.

Come along for a read - and go vote!

On Monday, I spent time in Dearborn - the hometown of Ford Motor Company and
the city with proportionally the largest Muslim population in the country.
There, I met Michigan state Rep. Alabas Farhat, who I was surprised to learn
was one year my younger, 26.

He invited me to join him at Al Ameer - a longtime local favorite that's
hosted the likes of Bill Clinton (who, once upon a time,
[encouraged](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cUoc2U6vcnI) a valedictorian
Abdul El-Sayed to run for office). Farhat was quick to point to the portrait
of Clinton's 2016 visit on the wall the moment we stepped inside.

We shared a table's worth of tomatoes and cucumbers and hummus and pita and
fresh falafel and mujaddara, and talked about Muslim-sounding names and Nazis
and which gets more scrutiny in the United States of America.

The meal was one of a series of conversations I had with Muslim and Arab
Americans, to listen to their experiences of living in a nation governed by a
political party that largely hates them, overseen by a man who has sought to
ban and criminalize and deport and bomb people who look like them.

We had these conversations near the end of a long and heated election season
that's seen vicious racism and Islamophobia hurled not just at Michigan
Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, but at the hundreds of thousands
of people in the state who look or pray like him.
